sentences.text: Maxakalisaurus was a medium-sized titanosaur, a group of large, long-necked herbivorous dinosaurs. It possessed a long neck and tail, along with ridged teeth, a feature that was unusual among sauropods. The animal also had osteoderms, which are bony deposits in the skin, a trait shared by many other titanosaurs.

The type specimen represents an animal approximately 12.1 meters long and weighing an estimated 5 tons. However, a separate juvenile specimen was estimated at 13 meters long and 9 tons, suggesting that adults may have reached 20 meters.
Alexander Kellner stated that Maxakalisaurus is the largest dinosaur ever described in Brazil.

The genus Maxakalisaurus was discovered in 1998 in the Adamantina Formation of Minas Gerais, Brazil. Alexander W. A. Kellner and his team formally described Maxakalisaurus topai as a new genus and species in 2006.

Excavations for the holotype skeleton took place between 1998 and 2002 along a road 45 km west of Prata, Minas Gerais. The holotype specimen, cataloged as MN 5013-V, was housed at the National Museum of Brazil. Fossils recovered from the type locality include remains belonging to both an adult and a subadult individual.
The genus name honors the Maxakali tribe, while the species name refers to their deity Topa. A new specimen containing a dentary and teeth was described as belonging to Maxakalisaurus in 2016.
South American sauropods, including Maxakalisaurus, evolved greater diversity and unusual traits due to a lack of significant competition.
Researchers have found bones that appear to belong to larger dinosaurs in Brazil, but these have not yet been assembled for scientific description.
